privateRecordSchemas.title: Optional private adult intimacy journal

restrictions: no legal names or contact identifiers
not evaluated by AI by default
No phone, email, social handle, contact ID, exact address, or identifying photo
store locally encrypted when implemented; sync separately opt-in
optional self-defined private trend scoring only after explicit opt-in; never automatic reward per encounter
do not infer from frequency or duration
local encrypted storage required before entry
no identifying information about another person

storagePolicy.aiProcessing: disabled_by_default; private sexual records/fantasies never sent to any AI provider unless a future separate explicit per-entry consent flow, data minimization, provider disclosure, and policy review are implemented
storagePolicy.exports: explicit user action and preview required
storagePolicy.deletion: user-accessible delete control; deletion results reconciled with backend if sync has been enabled
storagePolicy.scorecard: A private domain score may use only explicitly selected, user-entered self-ratings or descriptive trend fields and a stated personal goal. Raw intimate content is not shown in ordinary progress history and is never public.

scorePolicy.taskPoints: Optional reflection task can award its catalog-defined points for completing the reflection flow; sensitive answer content is not graded.
scorePolicy.xp: The reflection task may award its fixed task reward once per assignment; sexual activity itself is not a reward trigger.
scorePolicy.skillXp: May apply only to consent literacy, communication, self-awareness, or health-literacy tasks with explicit rubric.
scorePolicy.privateDomainScore: Optional adult_intimacy_wellbeing score based on user-reported consent knowledge, agency, comfort, communication, satisfaction, and chosen wellbeing goals.
scorePolicy.reason: Sexual wellbeing can be part of whole-life wellness. Keep optional adult data descriptive and private, permit explicitly selected personal trends, and never incentivize unwanted activity or reward disclosure itself.

userDefinedPrivateMetrics.purpose: Optional descriptive trends and a private, user-defined wellbeing goal. The player may choose to include or exclude any field.
userDefinedPrivateMetrics.scoring: A private domain trend may compare user-entered fields with a goal the adult player explicitly selected. Never convert those values into universal moral/health judgements, automatic task points, sexual-performance claims, or public ranks. Show that data is self-reported.
userDefinedPrivateMetrics.privacy: Local encrypted storage and opt-in sync must be implemented before storing sensitive journal text in production; no AI processing by default.
userDefinedPrivateMetrics.fieldNote: An adult may voluntarily record approximate first and most recent activity timing, optional frequency/encounter and partner-count estimates, optional duration, optional self-selected activity category, and user-created aliases. These are self-reported and stay private. The selected private trend may compare only fields selected by the user against a goal the user wrote; no universal good/bad or performance rating, no automatic per-act XP, and no AI processing by default.

privateRecordSchemas.verification: All entries remain self-reported; no partner identity or sexual activity is independently verified.

requiredFlow.rule: Check task ID/version, user consent, age eligibility, and allowed artifact type.
Create a preview and remove unnecessary names, exact location, account secrets, family images, intimate records, and unrelated health information.
Use only an installed and allowlisted provider/model adapter; a model name typed by the user alone is not enough.
Show which provider receives the submitted content, provider settings/billing caveat, and whether content may leave the device; require explicit confirmation.
Send only task-appropriate minimum inputs with a fixed rubric and strict output schema.
Validate returned JSON, rubric ID/version, bounded values, and required fields; reject malformed responses.
Run domain-engine rules separately. The model cannot override a failed prerequisite, evidence rule, safety check, eligibility rule, or server authorization.
Show the feedback and allow accept, edit, dismiss, or request another review. AI output is advice, not a fact by default.
Only the registered task policy plus authoritative backend acceptance can award permanent progression.
Store minimal provider/model/rubric/version/result metadata; do not log API keys; expose review/delete controls for AI artifacts.

allowedUses: check required fields in user-authored plans
evaluate a non-sensitive artifact against a fixed, versioned rubric
summarize records already provided by the user with provenance
help compare a plan against explicit user-stated constraints
explain a private score snapshot using its actual evidence references and rubric version
evaluate an opted-in personal presentation artifact against criteria written by the user, returning subjective suggestions rather than objective beauty claims
summarize an adult user-selected private wellbeing trend only after explicit per-task consent and data-scope preview, if the registered adapter permits the data class
help compare a user-selected values/faith practice goal or food plan against criteria the user explicitly chose, without inferring identity or ranking traditions
help explain contextual effort adjustments using registered deterministic reasons
prohibitedUses: inventing that an offline real-world action happened or treating an AI opinion as evidence of external facts
diagnosing or treating medical or mental-health conditions, or replacing qualified professional assessment

inferring religion, gender identity, sex-related anatomy, sexual orientation, disability, personality, morality, consent, or medical status from face/body images, meals, names, clothing, voice or behavior
claiming objective beauty, personality, morality, health, body-fat percentage or bone density from face structure or ordinary photographs

grading private sexual history or intimate details without explicit adult opt-in and a declared private rubric; never awarding task points simply for sexual acts, partner count, encounter count or duration
making identity-group rankings or declaring any religion, gender, orientation, disability status, body type, skin tone or socioeconomic group inherently better or worse
automatic publication, exact-address sharing, or sending a letter/media item without preview and confirmation
bypassing deterministic verification or granting authoritative rewards by itself
processing private intimacy journal entries, secrets, exact location, family media or raw keys by default
aiVerificationFramework.offlineBehavior: The deterministic game engine remains usable. AI-based review remains pending or unavailable unless an approved local model adapter is installed; do not fabricate a pass.

keyStorage.mobile: Use the actual platform secure-store adapter (Expo SecureStore on supported native platforms if installed/configured). Store only small secrets; handle keychain/keystore failures explicitly.
keyStorage.web: No equivalent secure store is assumed. Default to session-memory-only credentials. Never persist a raw key in localStorage or include it in sync; do not claim secure persistent BYOK on web without a separately reviewed implementation.
keyStorage.server: BYOK keys must not be transmitted to Thrivefold backend or included in task/telemetry/crash events. Server-configured provider secrets are a separate server-admin feature.
keyStorage.logs: Redact authorization headers, request URLs containing secrets, provider errors, prompt values that may include sensitive data, and crash breadcrumbs.
keyStorage.revocation: Provide remove/revoke action, clear in-memory caches, and require a fresh test after replacement.

scorecardIntegration.allowedInput: Minimum selected evidence and explicit user-defined rubric; provider and destination shown in a preview.
scorecardIntegration.authority: The deterministic scoring service and authorized backend are the only authorities for permanent scores, task points, XP, grace points and unlocks.
scorecardIntegration.userControl: User can accept, edit, dismiss or request a manual path; persist consent and rule version.
scorecardIntegration.sensitiveDomains: Adult intimacy, sexual history, exact location, family images, private letters and mental-health journals are excluded unless each supported feature has an implemented per-entry consent gate, redaction, provider disclosure and secure storage policy.
scorecardIntegration.gracePoints: AI may suggest a rationale only; only deterministic context-grace-v1 rules calculate the final bonus.

capabilities: estimate task-specific joint angles or repetition events where the registered implementation supports them
summarize landmark confidence and valid frame count
compare supported task-specific pose metrics with the player’s own prior comparable session where consented
support accessible/manual alternatives and confidence reporting
produce a private posture or movement-technique progress dimension only for explicitly registered metrics
nonCapabilities: measure bone density or body fat
prove that a user performed an activity whenever the person is out of frame
infer religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, personality, intentions, or morality
estimate exact body-fat percentage, bone density, or medical conditions from pose/image
provide universal attractiveness or physique rankings
poseLandmarkVerification.privacyDefaults: Use on-device processing, do not retain raw frames, do not upload raw video, and store only task-specific derived metrics and model/version metadata unless a separate explicit feature consent authorizes otherwise.
availabilityGate: camera permission is requested only at feature use
privacy test confirms raw frames are not persisted/uploaded by default
poseLandmarkVerification.ifUnavailable: Hide pose-verified reward pathway and offer an honestly classified no-camera alternative; never treat manual confirmation as landmark-verified.

principles: score real tasks and user-selected goals rather than identity disclosure
on-device processing by default for sensitive media where the adapter supports it

exactAddress.collection: May be stored only through a distinct, user-initiated private safety/contact feature with explicit purpose; never required for a game task.
exactAddress.use: The user may review or share an exact address with a specifically selected trusted recipient if the app implements a secure sharing flow and the user confirms recipient and contents.
exactAddress.gameRewards: No reward for revealing the address itself; a privacy/safety review task may award points for completing the review.
exactAddress.publicSharing: Never by default; warn before public or broad audience selection.
exactAddress.aiUse: Excluded by default; redact from provider prompts unless the user explicitly approves a specific necessary use.

homeAndFamilyPhotos.collection: Optional user-selected task or private archive; not required for game progress.
homeAndFamilyPhotos.picker: Use operating-system photo picker/single-selected asset picker; request broad library access only if a genuine gallery feature requires it and after a separate explanation.
homeAndFamilyPhotos.processing: On-device default where supported; preserve provenance and do not claim image inference if no tested adapter exists.
homeAndFamilyPhotos.sharing: Explicit per-item audience confirmation and review of what is visible; family/third-party privacy considered.
homeAndFamilyPhotos.metadata: Strip EXIF geolocation and unnecessary metadata before a consented upload.
homeAndFamilyPhotos.aiUse: Off by default for private/family media; no inference of religion, gender, orientation, morality, or diagnosis from images.
homeAndFamilyPhotos.progressPhotos: Opt-in comparison against the player’s own user-defined baseline; no exact body-fat/bone-density inference and no universal beauty ranking.

screenshots.redaction: remove addresses, names, access tokens, health records, intimate details, and private conversations before any share
screenshots.secretDetection: registered deterministic scanner may warn but does not guarantee all sensitive content was found

sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.galleryPermission: Use the operating-system photo picker for user-selected assets. Do not request broad all-gallery permission to complete tasks. A separate library management product feature may request the platform-supported scoped permission with an explanation and revocation control.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.cameraPermission: Request camera access only when the player explicitly starts an enabled camera task; provide a non-camera/manual alternative whenever feasible. Do not retain raw video frames by default.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.preciseLocation: Exact location is never a generic task requirement. A separate safety feature may store or share it only under explicit user control and clear recipient confirmation.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.contacts: Never import or scrape address books, match partners, or collect another person’s contact details as a task. Use a user-created private alias for optional journals.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.privateHealthAndIntimacy: High-sensitivity records stay separate from public profiles, default AI requests, analytics, and ordinary coaching. Adult intimacy records are locally encrypted where implemented; cloud sync requires separate explicit consent.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.thirdPartyData: Tasks must not pressure users to upload private messages, partner identities, family photos, home interiors, or another person’s health information.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.productionRequirement: Enforce this policy in UI, runtime capabilities, database RLS, sync, telemetry, and backend endpoints; JSON alone is not an access-control boundary.

scorecardPrivacy.sensitiveInput: do not put source values in reward ledger; store minimal reason codes and references

inputsAllowed: relevant user-recorded measurements with source and date
explicit user-selected identity/self-discovery goals where requested
user-selected faith, values, or dietary practices
age band when relevant to content or challenge calibration
user-selected disability/accessibility accommodations without diagnosis proof
optional work, housework, caregiving and exertion logs
personal functional baseline and supported landmark metrics
user-defined appearance/style goals and optional locally processed progress media
optional private adult wellbeing reflections after backend age gate
inputsProhibitedAsSoleBasis: unconfirmed sensitive identity inferred from face, name, food, clothes, voice, or behavior
medical diagnosis inferred from appearance, check-ins, or AI summaries
exact wealth inferred from occupation, address, or social media
sexual consent, orientation, satisfaction, or partner history inferred from images or other people’s data
body-fat percentage or bone density inferred from a face/body photo
rules: Direct self-declared gender, sex-related health context, orientation, religion/faith, dietary choices, disability/accessibility preferences, age band, work/caregiving load, and relationship goals may be used for relevant user-requested task personalization.

Use direct self-declaration for sensitive identity and private health context; do not infer religion from food, gender from appearance, sexual orientation from behavior, or health diagnoses from face structure.

Task and private domain scores may cover user-selected identity-support goals, faith/values practice, dietary preference alignment, relationships, adult wellbeing reflection, measurements, personal presentation, and financial/self-management goals using explicit rubrics.
A score reflects a task, action, goal, trend, or self-reported wellbeing dimension—not the inherent value of the user or a group.

Account for paid work, household labour, caregiving, standing, manual work, lifting, and other workload before assigning extra exercise. A high load can count toward activity dimensions and cause rest/adaptation recommendations.
Use personal baselines and accessible equivalent criteria. Older users and users who select disability/health adaptations may receive task-specific contextual grace points under context-grace-v1.
User-chosen dietary or faith/values tasks may receive the same configured values-alignment reward no matter which practice is selected. Never award for an identity label by itself.
Adult relationship/intimacy tasks are optional, private, consent-centered, and must never require sexual activity, dating success, or another person response.
User-selected photos may be used in local progress or style tasks only with explicit consent and registered adapters. Do not infer sensitive traits, diagnoses, or morality from face/body features.
Show why a task or score was selected and allow correction, pause, removal, or opt-out for each optional context.

Every supported contextual score dimension can be selected as a private scorecard domain. Sensitive dimensions are opt-in. Personalization may use explicit context; it may not infer religion, gender, orientation, disability, body composition, diagnosis or character from proxy signals.

Contextual grace may affect the task-specific reward only when a versioned task definition explicitly enables it and the adapted objective plus verification policy pass; setup/disclosure tasks do not get grace simply for collecting context.
User-selected values/dietary routes may receive the configured encouragement bonus after actual task completion. Equivalent authored paths use equivalent difficulty and evidence standards.

Personal appearance, body, oral appearance, identity, faith, mindset, character, finance and adult-intimacy dimensions must display their subjective/self-reported/measurement evidence type and remain private until separately shared.
taskPersonalizationRules.toneRule: Tone profiles change only wording. They never change objectives, evidence, base rewards, contextual adjustments, consent, eligibility, or verification.

optionalPrivateHistoryFields: first experience approximate date/age if user explicitly wishes
optional private fantasy/secret journal text (local encrypted storage, adult-only, AI off by default)
rules: Adult features require the backend-verified age gate and explicit feature opt-in; all questions can be skipped.
Private history may include approximate date, self-reported activity count/duration, or a user-created alias only if the adult user explicitly chooses those fields.
The private adult intimacy wellbeing domain may score self-reported consent knowledge, agency, communication, comfort, satisfaction, and completion of a chosen reflection task.

Raw partner count, encounter count, first-experience age, intercourse duration and frequency do not automatically award task points/XP or public leaderboard status. An adult may explicitly select private descriptive trend scoring against a personally defined goal; these self-reported values are not universal measures of sexual skill, morality or health.
Do not collect real partner names, phone numbers, contact IDs, social handles, exact location, or partner photos for game scoring.
No default AI processing, analytics capture, notification text, or public profile display for sexual records, fantasies, secrets, or intimate reflections.
Keep local encrypted storage as the default where implemented; cloud sync or AI processing requires a separate explicit consent flow and a security-reviewed implementation.

Dating/social tasks can reward task completion, planning, boundaries, consent literacy, and communication practice. They never require a hookup, sex, stranger approach, or another person accepting an invitation.
Consent, communication, and satisfaction are wellbeing dimensions; no one should be pressured to create a sexual experience for game points.

Thrivefold may provide coaching and structured reflection but must not misrepresent its AI as a licensed therapist, doctor, or marriage counselor. When appropriate, help the user prepare for qualified professional support.
intimacyAndRelationshipRules.relationshipSupportBoundary: Offer relationship-coaching prompts, communication practice, boundary planning, and referral preparation. Do not claim professional licensure or encourage coercion, surveillance, confrontation in unsafe situations, or disclosure of another person’s private information.

allowedToVary: task title phrasing within approved content variants
neverVary: score formulas and contextual bonus caps
taskPresentationRules.adultToneGate: cheeky_adult available only after an authoritative adult eligibility check; no explicit sexual coercion, shame, or pressure.

capabilities.releaseGate: must make a real minimal provider request; unavailable means no verified completion
must pass native secure-storage read/write/delete and telemetry-redaction tests
must enforce strict structured output and fixed deterministic rubrics
must pass real device, landmark-confidence, camera-permission, offline, and raw-frame retention tests
use user-selected assets; do not demand broad library access by default
strip EXIF GPS and validate preview before upload
verify actual save, audience, publish consent, and delete flows
use a synthetic practice fixture until actual redaction is available
adult gate, private storage, disabled AI by default, no-score enforcement, and delete/export controls must pass review
verify actual saved choice without sending a provider request
verify saved review state without needing an uploaded image
persist topic and selected outcome without storing prohibited sensitive values
use synthetic content and confirm redaction was applied before save
settings review available without contact import
adult eligibility, no-score policy, privacy controls, and opt-in state must pass tests
assessment ID, version, rubric, questions, answer key, and thresholds must actually exist; never pass an absent assessment
Persist versioned per-domain score snapshots, evidence references, visible weights, privacy, correction and disable flows; backend remains authoritative.
Deterministic versioned cap, reason code, overlap deduplication, adaptation checks and recovery-aware recommendations pass integration tests.
18+ gate, opt-in, local encrypted storage, data minimization, user-defined private trend rules, AI exclusion by default, RLS and delete/export behavior pass review.
OS picker, explicit camera/media consent, tested local adapter, no raw-frame retention/upload by default, accessible no-photo fallback and user deletion controls.
Rubric uses user-selected criteria and private self-baseline; does not infer personality, morality, health, race, gender, orientation or human worth.
Registered provider/model, consent preview, strict JSON output validation, deterministic score gate, secure key storage, no key/log leakage and no unsupported success.

runtimeCapabilityRegistry.fallback: Never label an unsupported capability as verified. Offer a relevant, accurately classified alternate task or hide the task until implemented. The personal scorecard must show unavailable or local-only provisional status when its engine is absent; never fabricate a score snapshot. If photo/face processing is unavailable, offer a manual self-rating or skip. If secure encrypted storage and age gating for adult intimate records are unavailable, do not collect or persist those fields.

fallbackByCapability.private_multidomain_scorecard_engine: No score is displayed as calculated unless the actual formula, evidence sources, ruleset version and persistence succeed.
fallbackByCapability.context_grace_and_workload_accounting: Keep base rewards only when valid; do not issue contextual bonuses until deterministic cap, context basis and duplicate-workload checks pass.
fallbackByCapability.private_adult_intimacy_records_v3: If adult eligibility, explicit consent, encrypted storage and deletion controls are not implemented, do not collect those private fields.
fallbackByCapability.local_personal_photo_progress_adapter: If model or local processing capability is unavailable, mark the task unavailable and offer a manual task; never claim photo analysis occurred.
fallbackByCapability.subjective_presentation_rubric: If the subjective rubric is unavailable, allow the user to record their own rating without an automated appearance score.
fallbackByCapability.ai_scorecard_rubric_adapter: If the provider is unavailable, continue with deterministic rubric/manual review and never fabricate an AI result.

rules: A special quest selects/assigns an eligible child task from its listed taskIds.
The child task must pass its own verification policy.
The child task award is the sole source of taskPoints, XP, and skill XP unless a separately authored quest bonus is configured and validated.
The quest-parent completion event never duplicates child rewards.
Daily point contribution uses the child task’s frozen reward snapshot and eligible date, not both parent and child values.
Quest acceptance, skip, replacement, or abandonment awards nothing.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: A deterministic app/backend event or registered evaluator passed its explicit rules. The verified scope is only what the evidence proves.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only after applicable authoritative reward processing.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: Evidence met format and rubric requirements, but the app cannot independently establish every real-world claim.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only under the task policy; present limitations plainly.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: The player attested to an offline or external action that the app cannot independently prove.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only if the catalog explicitly permits self-reported reward; never label it system-verified.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: A registered AI adapter reviewed a user-authored artifact against a fixed rubric; deterministic rules still govern eligibility and completion.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: AI output never awards authoritative progress by itself.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: An installed on-device sensor/model generated task-specific evidence with recorded confidence and limitations.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only for the specified detectable signal; not a medical diagnosis or proof beyond the model’s capability.

newFeatureAcceptanceTests.assertion: AI provider adapter must be registered and make a real non-sensitive connection test; no mocked success.
BYOK secret never appears in task evidence, logs, telemetry, analytics, prompts sent to another provider, or backend profile records.
AI review cannot verify external real-world activities or independently award XP/points.
Pose-landmark task is unavailable unless the installed model, native adapter, camera consent, and deterministic movement evaluator are available.
Raw frames/video are not retained or uploaded by default; confidence failures offer a non-camera alternative.
Exact address, home images, family photos, contacts, and private sexual-history fields are never required for task completion or rewards.
Media use is scoped to selected assets; preview and explicit audience consent precede sharing; upload metadata is sanitized.

Private intimacy history is adult-only, explicit opt-in, not publicly visible, excluded from AI by default, and may inform a private user-defined trend score only when the adult explicitly opts in. Raw activity values do not automatically grant task points/XP.
Changing tone profile changes only copy, not tasks, evidence, points, privacy, safety, or eligibility.
Social/dating tasks reward a qualifying plan or learning objective, never another person’s response, consent, or sexual activity.
Selected domains can be independently enabled, configured, scored using a versioned rubric, inspected against source event IDs, and disabled without deleting unrelated history.
Optional composite progress score uses only user-selected domains and displayed weights; missing or unselected domains are not silently treated as zero.

User-declared faith, gender identity, sex-related context, sexual orientation, dietary preferences, disability, age, occupation or wealth context can personalize relevant selected tasks; disclosure alone adds no points or penalty.
Contextual grace bonus requires an eligible adapted objective, successful verification, a reason code and the configured maximum cap; a profile field alone never awards a bonus.
Paid work, housework, cooking, gardening, carrying, standing and caregiving activity can update workload scoring and influence whether further exercise is suggested; overlapping time is deduplicated.
Movement results, including a supported jump/reach task, compare only with a compatible personal baseline and explicitly record measurement method, adaptation and confidence.
Personal presentation and optional face-style scoring use player-defined subjective criteria; no universal beauty rank or face-based inference about personality, morality or health is shown.
A player can score progress toward self-defined identity, confidence, expression, or support goals without disclosing an identity; no identity group is ranked as inherently better or worse.
Faith/cultural/vegetarian/halal/kosher/vegan and other selected food paths can be scored for completed chosen actions under the same effort/verification framework; religion is not inferred from food.

Adult self-reported first/recent activity timing, optional encounter/partner counts and duration can be stored privately after explicit opt-in; private trend scoring is user-defined and never automatically rewards more activity.
The coach may reduce or replace a workout after a high-workload/caregiving day; the player can select rest or a lower-impact equivalent without a penalty.
AI score assistance receives only selected evidence and a versioned rubric after preview/consent; deterministic code and the backend decide permanent score/reward outcomes.
Selected progress images use the OS picker; on-device adapter status is checked, and unavailable capabilities produce an honest fallback rather than a fake verified pass.
Exact address, family photos, intimate records, private letters, and API keys are never mandatory task evidence or automatically submitted to AI.
Beast/God/Shadow/Devil/Adult-Honest tones affect wording only and never weaken verification, privacy, consent, age gating, safety, or reward rules.
Every production task has a registered domain score rubric and all referenced score dimensions resolve.
Every chapter capstone references valid task IDs, a registered verification policy, and a once-only milestone reward; every 50-level checkpoint resolves.
The domain score is calculated from actual source events using the stored rubric version and remains separate from task points/XP.
Contextual grace points are computed deterministically, reason-coded, capped at 25% of eligible base task points, and not duplicated on sync retries.
Sensitive context can personalize and score an opted-in goal, but disclosing the identity or field alone cannot create a score or reward.
Adult self-reported activity fields can support only a private user-defined trend after explicit opt-in; no activity count directly triggers task XP or public ranking.
Every level references only existing chapter tasks eligible at that level; all 20 chapter capstones and the final level-1000 milestone resolve.
The schema has no blanket deny-list for supported score domains; every supported domain has an explicit method, provenance class and applicable rubric.

Private user-selected scorecards support the explicit religion/faith, gender identity, sex-related context, sexual-orientation self-discovery, adult activity trend, mindset, character, appearance/style, body, oral-health and accessibility dimensions with opt-in controls.
Sensitive fields are not inferred from meal, clothing, face, name, voice, location, photos or behavior; directly declared context may drive user-requested personalization.
Selected dietary/faith/value task variants apply the configured equivalent encouragement bonus after valid completion, never for profile disclosure alone.

Physical work, housework, cooking, gardening and caregiving can count as relevant activity/load, overlapping periods are deduplicated, and heavy days can trigger recovery rather than redundant exercise.
Optional adult intimate-history trends require age eligibility and per-domain opt-in, are marked self-reported/private, and do not trigger automatic per-act rewards.

Beauty, face-shape, skin-tone styling, body-shape and tooth-appearance dimensions use user-defined subjective criteria or valid source measurements; no unsupported diagnosis or personality inference is made.
Every level references valid task content and valid score dimensions under the current scorecard ruleset, with capstones at every 50-level boundary.

contextualScoringFramework.purpose: Score what the player does, how the player is progressing against their own goals, and how task difficulty should be adapted to actual life context.
contextualScoringFramework.missingDataBehavior: null_not_zero; show_insufficient_data until a user opts in and enough valid records exist

scoreDimensions.title: Accessibility, adaptation and relative effort
scoreDimensions.method: Score the adapted objective and progress against the player’s baseline. Eligible additional effort can receive the bounded grace bonus; the disability label or disclosure alone does not.

scoreDimensions.title: Private intimacy wellbeing
scoreDimensions.method: Private adult score may include consent knowledge, agency, communication, comfort, satisfaction and the completion of a chosen wellbeing goal. Raw sexual-history fields may be included only in a separate explicitly selected self-reported trend dimension; no automatic per-act rewards, public comparisons or claims of clinical sexual performance.

scoreDimensions.title: Adult sexual-history trends (private, optional)
scoreDimensions.method: Only activated by an adult who explicitly opts in. Values are self-reported and descriptive; a private score can compare selected fields against a user-defined personal target if the player requests it. Higher frequency, partner count, first-sex age, or duration is not inherently better and never automatically grants task points, XP, public rank or claims of sexual skill. Missing data remains unknown.

scoreDimensions.title: Age and life-stage calibrated progress
scoreDimensions.method: Use age only when the task rules require it for eligibility or a relevant adaptation. Score completion and relative progress with an appropriately calibrated objective; age alone is not an ability score or automatic bonus.

scoreDimensions.title: AI literacy and responsible tool use
scoreDimensions.method: Score demonstrated setup and safe use; never award points for revealing an API key.

scoreDimensions.title: Personal aesthetic goals (subjective)
scoreDimensions.method: Private and subjective. Score the player’s own changeable appearance/presentation goals and choices; do not produce a universal attractiveness rank or infer personality, health or morality.

scoreDimensions.title: Body metrics and functional goals
scoreDimensions.method: Compare with the user’s baseline and chosen goal; never infer body fat or bone density from photos; no compulsory weight loss.

scoreDimensions.title: Values in action
scoreDimensions.method: Reflect consistency with user-selected principles; no universal moral-character verdict.

scoreDimensions.title: Communication and learning
scoreDimensions.method: Score practice and progress against the learner’s starting point, not accent or native-speaker status.

scoreDimensions.title: Education and self-directed learning
scoreDimensions.method: Score actual learning, practice and progress relative to the chosen goal; never rank formal education level or socioeconomic access as human worth.

scoreDimensions.title: Financial self-management
scoreDimensions.method: Score chosen financial behaviours and personal targets; raw wealth is not a leaderboard metric.

scoreDimensions.title: Gender identity support and self-defined expression
scoreDimensions.method: Private and optional. Score progress on a user-selected expression, confidence, support-seeking or wellbeing goal; a gender label itself does not earn or lose points. Never infer identity from images or behavior.

scoreDimensions.title: Habits and follow-through
scoreDimensions.method: Score defined actions, user-selected targets, and improvement over personal baseline; never punish rest or a skipped task.

scoreDimensions.title: Health and everyday function
scoreDimensions.method: Score record quality, functional progress, and completion of chosen health-management tasks; not diagnosis or body worth.

scoreDimensions.title: Household work and caregiving contribution
scoreDimensions.method: Credit supported reports of cooking, cleaning, carrying, caregiving, standing and other work toward workload planning. Avoid exact calorie claims and duplicate time windows; use the load to adapt the day’s challenge.

scoreDimensions.title: Identity, self-discovery and self-defined expression
scoreDimensions.method: Score progress on user-selected self-discovery, expression, confidence, support-seeking or wellbeing goals. A self-declared identity can select relevant content; identity disclosure alone is not a score and the rubric must not assert that one identity is superior.

scoreDimensions.title: Mindset and self-awareness
scoreDimensions.method: Score engagement and personal trend only; never diagnose or assign mental worth.

scoreDimensions.title: Movement and total physical workload
scoreDimensions.method: Count relevant safe movement/workload from all sources; normalize to personal capacity and recovery needs; avoid double-counting overlapping activity.

scoreDimensions.title: Nutrition and chosen food goals
scoreDimensions.method: Score completion of the player’s chosen feasible nutrition actions; no diet morality rank and no deduction for food insecurity.

scoreDimensions.title: Dental and oral-care routines
scoreDimensions.method: Score routines and care follow-through; no diagnosis or moral ranking from tooth colour.

scoreDimensions.title: Personal style and presentation
scoreDimensions.method: Private, subjective progress against the player’s own criteria, not a universal beauty or attractiveness ranking.

scoreDimensions.title: Personality preferences and behavior goals
scoreDimensions.method: Score progress against specific changeable behaviors and the player’s self-defined working preferences. Do not infer personality, intelligence, honesty or morality from face structure, voice, name or a single behavior.

scoreDimensions.title: Posture and movement technique
scoreDimensions.method: Use only task-specific metrics supported by an installed model; no diagnosis or fitness claim beyond tested criteria.

scoreDimensions.title: Public presence, presentation and professional communication
scoreDimensions.method: Score practice and progress against the player’s own criteria for speaking, interviews, workplace/school presentations or public-facing communication. Do not infer value from accent, social status, follower counts or appearance, and never require public posting.

scoreDimensions.title: Relationships and social confidence
scoreDimensions.method: Score practice and personally defined progress; another person’s refusal or lack of response never lowers a score.

scoreDimensions.title: Sex-related health context and relevant care goals
scoreDimensions.method: Use user-declared context only where relevant to a selected health workflow. Score education, record quality, functional outcomes or chosen care-management actions; do not rate sex assigned at birth as a personal merit.

scoreDimensions.title: Sexual-orientation self-discovery and affirming wellbeing
scoreDimensions.method: Private and optional. Score a self-defined goal such as learning, self-acceptance, expression, support or relationship communication; never rank orientations or infer one from behavior.

scoreDimensions.title: User-selected colour and styling preferences
scoreDimensions.method: Score subjective fit to the player’s chosen colour/style goals. Never score skin tone as superior or inferior, infer race/health from tone, or recommend skin-lightening as a value judgement.

scoreDimensions.title: Social confidence and dating practice
scoreDimensions.method: Score preparation, communication, boundaries and self-defined confidence. Never reward coercion, another person’s response, a hookup, or acquiring a partner.

scoreDimensions.title: Values or faith practice
scoreDimensions.method: Score chosen practice completion or learning; no inference of belief and no ranking religions.

scoreDimensions.title: Religion and faith context (private, user-configured)
scoreDimensions.method: May contribute to a private user-selected scorecard through self-rated relevance, chosen practice, learning, observance planning or completion of a values-aligned task. An explicit declaration can provide context; it does not trigger automatic points. Values-alignment bonuses are based on a registered selected task and its evidence.

scoreDimensions.title: Gender identity context and self-defined goals
scoreDimensions.method: May be a selected private context dimension. Score only self-defined support, expression, confidence, learning or wellbeing goals using the player's rubric; identity labels do not imply a universal positive or negative score.

scoreDimensions.title: Sex-assigned-at-birth health context
scoreDimensions.method: An optional health-context dimension only when a user-selected feature clearly requires it. A private user-defined score may assess completion of chosen health-literacy or care-planning actions; the field itself does not automatically grant rewards or determine identity.

scoreDimensions.title: Sexual orientation and self-discovery context
scoreDimensions.method: May participate in an explicitly enabled private scorecard for user-selected self-discovery, support, communication or relationship goals. Never infer orientation from photos, messages, contacts or behavior; never automatically rate an orientation label as better or worse.

scoreDimensions.title: Adult sexual-activity history (private, optional)
scoreDimensions.method: Can feed an adult-only user-defined descriptive trend only after explicit opt-in. Raw activity, frequency, partner count, first experience age or duration do not automatically award points or imply skill. A private score follows the user's stated goal and disclosed rubric, not a universal more-is-better rule.

scoreDimensions.title: Mindset and self-evaluated wellbeing (not human worth)
scoreDimensions.method: The player may score and review their self-rated mindset, mood-related wellbeing, confidence, coping-practice completion and progress against their own goals. This is not a judgement of human worth and is not a diagnosis.

scoreDimensions.title: Character, commitments and repair
scoreDimensions.method: A private, user-defined reflection rubric may score alignment between a chosen value and a specific action, follow-through, acknowledgement of harm, and repair. It must not infer character from appearance, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, status, or a single AI opinion.

scoreDimensions.title: Personal beauty and aesthetic goals (subjective, user-defined)
scoreDimensions.method: The player may use their own explicit rubric for a private aesthetic or presentation goal. Any numeric rating must be labeled subjective and based on the player's declared criteria; it is not an objective human attractiveness ranking. Photo feedback requires a real enabled adapter and explicit image consent.

scoreDimensions.title: Face-shape and feature preferences
scoreDimensions.method: May score completion of a face-shape/style exploration goal and the player's chosen style criteria. A real feature-analysis adapter must be available before automated measurements; no personality, morality, intelligence, health diagnosis or sensitive identity can be inferred from facial structure.

scoreDimensions.title: Body-shape goals and personal comfort
scoreDimensions.method: Score completion of user-selected comfort, function, clothing-fit, movement or measurement-review goals using actual sourced measurements or self-report. Do not infer exact body composition from ordinary photos or equate one body shape with greater human value.

scoreDimensions.title: Skin tone and colour/style preferences
scoreDimensions.method: May score the player's progress on chosen colour styling, clothing, grooming or skin-care goals. Skin tone itself is not a quality score; no race or identity is inferred from a photo.

scoreDimensions.title: Oral appearance and dental-care goals
scoreDimensions.method: Score follow-through on a safe, user-selected oral-care or appearance goal and dental-care planning. Do not diagnose disease, measure tooth whiteness from images, or reward unsafe whitening practices. Clinical findings remain distinct from self-reported appearance.

scoreDimensions.title: Body-fat and body-composition records
scoreDimensions.method: Score record completeness, source quality, safe user-selected goal actions and longitudinal change only when comparable real measurements exist. Never derive body-fat percentage from face shape or an unvalidated image estimate; do not shame or reward weight change alone by default.

scoreDimensions.title: Disability, accessibility and adapted progress
scoreDimensions.method: May inform accessible alternatives, goal calibration, relative progress and bounded grace points when a registered adapted objective is completed. No diagnosis proof is required for ordinary accommodations. Disability disclosure alone is not a task or bonus trigger.

domainScoringAlgorithm.base: Score each domain separately using eligible, timestamped events and versioned rubrics.
domainScoringAlgorithm.overrides: Each domain may override weights with a versioned domain-specific rubric. Do not apply weights to missing data; renormalize remaining valid weights and disclose reduced confidence.
domainScoringAlgorithm.selfReport: Clearly label self-reported components and confidence; never disguise an attestation as sensor verification.
domainScoringAlgorithm.privacy: Store score snapshots with input event IDs, formula version, confidence, and visibility. Hide private domains from public profile and analytics by default.
domainScoringAlgorithm.explicitContextRule: User-selected sensitive context may define a private dimension or personalization input after informed opt-in. Use the applicable domain rubric and display its meaning, source, confidence and version. Do not infer the context from proxies.

identityAndContextUsage.age: Use for age-appropriate features and task calibration where relevant; no blanket claim of capability or incapability.
identityAndContextUsage.disability: User-selected accommodations and alternative objectives can activate grace eligibility; no diagnosis proof required for ordinary accessibility adaptations.
identityAndContextUsage.genderAndSexContext: Directly declared gender identity and sex-related context can be enabled as named private scorecard dimensions when the player selects them. The personal score may reflect a user-defined self-rating, expression/support goal, or relevant health-context goal. Use sex-related fields only in relevant user-selected health workflows; never infer anatomy from gender identity or apply universal group rankings.
identityAndContextUsage.sexualOrientation: A voluntarily supplied sexual-orientation/self-discovery context can be a private selected scorecard dimension and can tailor affirming tasks. The personal rubric measures a user-defined self-rating, support, self-discovery, communication or wellbeing goal; do not infer or rank orientations.
identityAndContextUsage.religionAndValues: Religion/faith context can be a named private scorecard dimension when the user directly declares it and opts in. Score only the user's selected personal rubric, self-rating, observance/learning practice or values-aligned actions. Configured encouragement bonuses may apply to completed selected faith, dietary or secular-values tasks under equivalent evidence rules; do not infer religion from food or compare traditions as inherently superior.
identityAndContextUsage.diet: Dietary choices can be scored when explicitly selected as personal goals. A registered task may give values-alignment/encouragement points for completing the selected vegetarian, vegan, halal, kosher, allergy-aware, cultural, religious or other diet path according to its actual objective and evidence. Never infer religion from a meal.
identityAndContextUsage.occupationAndHouseholdWork: Use reported physical demand and duration to recognise activity and reduce redundant exercise assignments.
identityAndContextUsage.healthContext: Use volunteered context to offer alternatives and safety notices, not to diagnose or change treatment.
identityAndContextUsage.character: Character-in-action may be a private user-defined reflection score based on specific chosen commitments, actions, follow-through and repair. Do not infer morality or intent from face structure, religion, gender, wealth or other proxy.
identityAndContextUsage.appearance: Beauty, face-shape, body-shape, skin-tone styling and oral-appearance goals can be private subjective dimensions using player-authored criteria, self-ratings and supported photo/measurement tools. Never present a subjective rubric as objective human worth or infer morality/personality from appearance.
identityAndContextUsage.mentalWellbeing: Mindset and wellbeing trends may be scored from optional self-reports and completed goal practices. Use as self-reported wellbeing/progress, never as a measure of human worth or as a diagnosis.

output.dimensionSelection: Each dimension is independently available to the user; high-sensitivity dimensions stay off until explicitly enabled.

antiGaming: No double counting one event in overlapping activities without explicit allocation.
No reward solely for submitting an attribute, photograph, diagnosis, or intimate detail.
Use assignment IDs, event IDs, time windows, and idempotency keys.
Reward genuine completion and skill progress; do not force sensitive disclosures.
All adjustment calculations are deterministic, auditable, and versioned.

userConfigurableCompositeScore.label: My selected progress score
userConfigurableCompositeScore.rule: The player may explicitly select and privately score any supported dimension, including religion/faith context, gender identity or expression, sex-related health context, sexual-orientation self-discovery, adult self-reported sexual-history trends, mental wellbeing, chosen character/repair rubric, subjective beauty/style/face-shape preferences, body shape/measurements, skin-tone styling preferences, oral-appearance goals, body-composition records, and disability/accessibility progress. The player chooses criteria and weights, sees the rubric, can pause or remove a dimension, and can keep dimensions private. Sensitive context must be explicitly supplied or self-rated; do not infer it from proxy attributes. A context score describes the configured personal rubric, not universal superiority or human worth.
userConfigurableCompositeScore.inputs: Only score snapshots from the selected domains with eligible evidence and disclosed confidence.
userConfigurableCompositeScore.sharing: requires separate explicit sharing action and audience preview
userConfigurableCompositeScore.defaultBehavior: Show scorecard dimensions for all applicable goals and records. Keep high-sensitivity dimensions disabled until the user opts in; do not invent values for unselected or missing data.
userConfigurableCompositeScore.title: Personal Progress Score
userConfigurableCompositeScore.contextFieldTreatment: User-declared religion, gender identity, sex-related context, orientation, age, disability/accessibility, dietary choices or other selected profile context may be used in a scorecard only if the player explicitly enables the relevant domain and chooses a meaningful scoring rubric. Context can change eligibility, comparison baseline, adaptations, or bonus rules; disclosure itself must never be secretly converted into a reward or penalty.

scoreableDomainHandling.default: Offer relevant domains, then let player select scoring dimensions and criteria. High-sensitivity domains are off until explicitly enabled.
scoreableDomainHandling.scoreType: Private per-domain score with source, rubric version, confidence, evidence class and comparison baseline where applicable.
scoreableDomainHandling.identityContext: Explicitly declared context may be a scored/private scorecard dimension when the player selects it; score meaning and criteria are shown. It must not be inferred from proxies.
scoreableDomainHandling.noGlobalGroupRanking: Personal scorecards are user-defined and private by default; do not compare groups by religion, gender, disability, skin tone, sexuality or other identity labels.
scoreableDomainHandling.editing: Editable, pauseable, and removable by the player; historical snapshots record the rubric version used.

defaultEnablement.ordinaryDomains: Offer relevant low-sensitivity domains by default after explaining the scoring model; allow the player to deselect any domain.
defaultEnablement.sensitiveRule: High-sensitivity domains are available but require explicit per-domain opt-in and private visibility by default.
defaultEnablement.noDataRule: No input is not a zero score; use insufficient_data until sufficient valid and permitted inputs exist.

religion_or_faith.bonusRule: A configured values-alignment task can award bounded effort bonus for completing its authored, higher-effort objective. The rule is applied equivalently to vegetarian, vegan, halal, kosher, allergy-aware, secular and other chosen food/value paths; no bonus is granted merely for profile disclosure.

gender_identity.bonusRule: A player may select a private identity-support/expression dimension and score a self-defined goal; no label is inferred or assigned a default quality.

sex_assigned_at_birth.bonusRule: Use only in a user-selected relevant health workflow; no identity-based reward or penalty.

sexual_orientation.bonusRule: Optional private goal-progression score only; never infer or rank orientations.

sexual_activity.bonusRule: Raw activity metrics can update a user-selected descriptive trend; task rewards apply only to completed educational/reflection tasks, not to sex, number of partners or another person's response.

mental_worth_and_mindset.bonusRule: Score the user's own reported wellbeing and goal progress; never treat the result as a score of human worth or a diagnosis.

moral_character_and_repair.bonusRule: Private score follows the user's explicit rubric for a specific action/commitment and repair; it does not infer a fixed moral trait from appearance, identity, or AI speculation.

beauty_or_attractiveness.bonusRule: A subjective personal score is permitted only against the user's chosen criteria. Do not present it as an objective human attractiveness ranking.

face_shape_and_features.bonusRule: Score completion and personal preference alignment; automated analysis remains unavailable unless a real model adapter exists and passes its tests.

body_shape.bonusRule: Use actual sourced measurements and user-selected personal goals; don't invent body composition from images.

skin_tone.bonusRule: Score selected styling goals, not inherent skin tone or a skin-tone hierarchy.

tooth_whiteness_and_oral_appearance.bonusRule: Score chosen safe care or appearance goals; do not recommend damaging whitening methods or claim image-based clinical diagnosis.

body_fat_and_composition.bonusRule: Only values with date, units, method and source can be treated as measurements. Weight/body-composition changes do not automatically grant or deduct XP.

disability_and_accessibility.bonusRule: A bounded grace bonus can be awarded for an eligible, completed adapted objective. A disability label alone is not the trigger; no diagnosis document is required for ordinary adaptations.

contextualGraceAndEffortRules.purpose: Ensure task difficulty and rewards acknowledge different capacities, age-related constraints, disability, pain, fatigue, language confidence, resources, occupational exertion, household labour, and caregiving.
contextualGraceAndEffortRules.principle: Offer equivalent objectives and extra effort credit when a task’s adapted/difficulty-calibrated version is genuinely challenging for this player. Do not require users to prove a diagnosis to receive ordinary accessibility support.

contextBonusPolicy.basePoints: Use the authored task reward snapshot.
contextBonusPolicy.whenEligible: Only when the registered task policy marks the alternative as context-calibrated and the task completion/evidence passes. A user may self-select relevant context without uploading proof.
contextBonusPolicy.ageAdjustment: Age may trigger a lower-impact equivalent or adaptive rubric on relevant physical/health tasks. Bonus reflects the validated adjusted objective, not a blanket age assumption.
contextBonusPolicy.accessibilityAdjustment: An accessible alternative can earn the same base reward; a registered contextual-effort bonus may apply when its rubric specifies additional effort or barriers.
contextBonusPolicy.highWorkloadAdjustment: Do not award bonus merely for reporting a job title. Record real activity/load and credit it in workload and movement dimensions; use it to reduce redundant exercise assignments. Bonus only when an explicitly defined challenge is completed.
contextBonusPolicy.languageAndResourceAdjustment: Offer equivalent language/access/resource routes. Apply any configured grace to the qualifying task, not to identity disclosure.
contextBonusPolicy.noProofBurden: Do not ask for diagnosis documents, employer letters, income proofs, or private medical records just to enable an accessible task.

effortBasedScoring.baseTaskReward: Always award the task’s authored base reward only after its verification policy passes.
effortBasedScoring.trigger: A task-specific, versioned rule confirms that the completed adapted objective required additional relative effort or accommodated barriers, and the evidence passes.
contextExamples: A user with a disability completes the supported equivalent objective with an explicitly registered adaptation.
An older user chooses and completes a relevant calibrated movement/health task appropriate to their own functional baseline.
A user whose work or caregiving already provides substantial physical load receives credit for that workload and may be offered recovery instead of extra exercise.
A user improves a registered jump/reach or mobility outcome relative to their own baseline; height may be used only as context or in a validated task-specific normalization.
A language learner improves against their own communication baseline regardless of accent, rural/urban background or educational history.
notTriggers: age alone without relevant task adaptation
effortBasedScoring.sameEventRules: Do not award the same exertion or event twice across movement/workload domains. Any additional domain credit must be a separate declared score calculation and not a duplicate XP event.

rules: A work or household activity can count as movement/load when the recorded duration and type support it.
Avoid double-counting the same time window across multiple logs.
Do not calculate precise calories from a job title or activity label alone.
If a validated device estimate exists, preserve provider and measurement provenance; otherwise display effort bands or broad estimates only.
Sexual activity may be logged by an adult user if they choose, but is not a recommended task and is not rewarded by frequency or partner count.
High physical workload may cause the coach to recommend rest, mobility, or non-exercise tasks instead of additional workouts.
activityCreditModel.noWorkoutAssumption: Do not assign ten push-ups or a workout solely because a player has not logged gym activity. First account for job, household work, caregiving, current function, and recovery.

relativePerformanceRules.baseline: Use the player’s own prior comparable attempts when consented and available.
relativePerformanceRules.comparison: Score improvement relative to baseline and task-specific safe criteria, with relevant context such as assistance, mobility aid, range of motion, and measurement method.
relativePerformanceRules.example: A shorter person who improves a jump-height or reach outcome relative to their own baseline can earn a meaningful improvement score; do not compare people using raw height alone.
relativePerformanceRules.limitations: Do not present an unvalidated video estimate as an exact medical or athletic measurement.
relativePerformanceRules.heightRule: A shorter player’s valid jump/reach improvement can earn a strong personal-progress score. Do not assign superiority or infer ability from height alone. If a height-normalized comparison is used, the exact formula and source value must be declared in a validated task definition; otherwise compare like-for-like personal measurements.

audit: Record ruleset, contextual flag codes, bonus amount, and task objective in the server ledger.
Do not store a sensitive diagnosis in a public reward receipt.
Same qualifying event must not receive a second bonus on sync retry.
Player can inspect why an adjustment applied and opt out of context-based personalization.
contextualGraceAndEffortRules.rule: Contextual grace is an optional, separately ledgered bonus (0-25%) for completion of a registered, evidence-valid task objective that explicitly permits adaptation or context-calibrated difficulty. The score engine may use declared age/life stage, accessibility, user-reported constraint, personal baseline, language confidence or recorded work/caregiving load when relevant to that task. The profile label itself never triggers a reward. The chosen adapted task, its validated objective and its reason code trigger the bonus.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: Task outcome and follow-through
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: Renormalize weights over eligible inputs only and reduce confidence; do not fill missing data with zero.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private 0-100 domain score contribution with a rule version, source event IDs, confidence and evidence class.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: Evidence and record quality
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: Missing required evidence fails task verification; optional unavailable measurements do not create a zero score.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private data-quality score contribution; not a medical conclusion.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: Relative personal progress
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: Without a comparable valid baseline, score task completion and record quality only; do not fabricate an improvement value.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private score contribution relative to the player’s own baseline; no unsupported population rank.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: Total workload and recovery-aware planning
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: Use broad effort bands unless a validated data source supplies a real estimate; do not fabricate calories.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private activity/workload score contribution and a plan recommendation; not an exact calorie/health diagnosis.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: User-defined appearance and presentation goal
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: Without a selected rubric, offer private self-rating only; do not create an objective beauty score.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private subjective style/presentation score using the player’s own criteria.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: Private adult wellbeing and self-selected trend
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: All optional fields may remain blank. For a user-selected raw activity trend, show only descriptive progress against the user-defined target, never an inherent good/bad rating or automatic task/XP multiplier.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private adult-only self-reported trend/score with an explicit data class and uncertainty.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: User-selected values, faith or dietary practice
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: A selected identity or preference alone earns no points; an unselected path is not a zero score.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private value-alignment/task score. The same difficulty and verification rules apply across faith, secular and dietary paths.

domainScoreRubricDefinitions.title: Self-reflection and chosen behavior change
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.missingInputHandling: Do not infer a diagnosis or moral trait from wording. Score the task structure and the user-selected goal/action only.
domainScoreRubricDefinitions.output: Private self-development score contribution, not a universal personality or moral-character verdict.

rewardPolicyDefinitions.purpose: Award the task definition’s frozen task points, XP and skill XP exactly once after its registered completion policy and verification gates pass.
rewardPolicyDefinitions.baseRewardSource: immutable task definition snapshot for the assigned task version
rewardPolicyDefinitions.ledger: append-only reward ledger with source completion event, ruleset version and unique idempotency key

rewardPolicyDefinitions.purpose: Award bounded contextual grace points only for a qualifying completed adapted objective or task-specific documented effort basis.
rewardPolicyDefinitions.baseRewardSource: verified-task-rewards-v1; grace is an additional separately ledgered component
requiredConditions: baseline/context inputs are permitted and current
disallowedTriggers: occupation title alone without activity load
rewardPolicyDefinitions.ledger: separate event with source completion event, policy version, reason code, bonus calculation and idempotency key

rewardPolicyDefinitions.purpose: Award a separate chapter milestone only after the chapter capstone requirements pass.
rewardPolicyDefinitions.reward: 20 task points and 35 XP once per capstone completion
requiredConditions: minimum distinct verified child tasks completed
all required task IDs are valid and eligible
disallowedTriggers: reusing the same event for multiple distinct tasks
rewardPolicyDefinitions.ledger: separate milestone reward entry with child event references

rewardPolicyDefinitions.purpose: Grant an optional once-per-game-date reward when eligible verified daily point contributions reach the saved target.
rewardPolicyDefinitions.ledger: one daily completion award per player, local game date and target ruleset version

rewardPolicyDefinitions.purpose: Update a private domain score snapshot from selected, permitted, versioned input events without automatically changing task points or XP.
disallowedTriggers: private record automatically sent to AI
rewardPolicyDefinitions.ledger: score snapshot with domain/rubric version, source event IDs, confidence and visibility; no task/XP award unless a separate task policy passes

rewardPolicyDefinitions.purpose: Prevent a special-quest parent from duplicating the reward already awarded by its completed child task.
rewardPolicyDefinitions.ledger: parent completion event references child completion ID and issues no duplicate child reward
